findings.title: Findings converge on run_scan's contract for a #52 second run
findings.why_it_matters: Three findings land on what run_scan promises a second run, and #52's two-tree shape is itself open.
findings.recommended: A: Re-evaluate run_scan's second-run contract before addressing Findings 2, 6, and 7
findings.chosen: A: Re-evaluate run_scan's second-run contract before addressing Findings 2, 6, and 7

findings.title: D3's #52 route relies on a symlink check whose verdict never reaches the base run
findings.why_it_matters: An explicit path skips the symlink guard, so a base run could write through a symlinked cache directory.
findings.recommended: A: Remove D3's #52 route: drop the explicit-path sentence and clause, and state that an explicit path is never vetted

findings.title: The file phase's output is undefined, and nothing owns source retention
findings.why_it_matters: Parent D14 relies on in-memory bytes that today live only within one loop iteration.
findings.recommended: A: Add a decision: the file phase returns the run's totals and keeps no sources, and retention is #59's to settle against parent D14
findings.chosen: A: Add a decision: the file phase returns the run's totals and keeps no sources, and retention is #59's to settle against parent D14

findings.title: D2 C's rewrite rests on cache tests that don't pin what it reorders
findings.why_it_matters: A mutation probe changed eight cache rules and six went unnoticed by the full suite.
findings.recommended: B: Keep D2 C, pin the six unpinned cache behaviours before the move, and land the move and the cache object as separate commits
findings.chosen: B: Keep D2 C, pin the six unpinned cache behaviours before the move, and land the move and the cache object as separate commits

findings.title: expanduser().resolve() has to move with cache resolution, unpinned today
findings.why_it_matters: Dropping it would create a literal ~ directory, and no test would notice.
findings.chosen: Summary names the move of cache-location resolution and adds relative and ~ --cache-dir pins

findings.title: Two runs would each get their own cache object over one directory
findings.why_it_matters: A second run over a broken directory warns twice and retries writes.
findings.recommended: B: Accept as a known limitation: each run_scan call owns its cache object, so a second run over a broken cache directory warns twice and retries writes

findings.title: config_path rides into run_scan only to be echoed into ScanResult
findings.why_it_matters: The engine's return type is tied to the CLI's rendering model.
findings.recommended: B: Accept as a known limitation: run_scan returns the CLI's ScanResult with config_path echoed, and #52 revisits it if a base run needs otherwise

findings.title: Cache-key helper moves with a hard-wired options list
Findings converge on who builds and owns RunCache
findings.why_it_matters: A flag passed twice, a lifecycle across two functions, and a position-dependent constructor all sit at the hand-off between run_scan and run_file_phase.
findings.recommended: B: Keep the current boundary and address Findings 2, 3 and 4 individually
findings.chosen: B: Keep the current boundary and address Findings 2, 3 and 4 individually

findings.title: debug enters the pipeline twice
findings.why_it_matters: The cache's replay rule and the scanner's tracebacks read separate inputs for one setting.
findings.recommended: C: Accept as a known limitation
findings.chosen: Move the replay rule to the loop
findings.choice_reason: User asked for more detail and saw it as a code smell rather than an edge case; this option was proposed in the walkthrough, not by synthesis.

findings.title: The cache lifecycle is split across run_scan and run_file_phase
findings.why_it_matters: Nothing at the call site shows the callee opens and closes the cache.
findings.recommended: C: Accept as a known limitation
findings.chosen: A: Keep construction in run_scan and move the prepare and finish calls there too

findings.title: RunCache.__init__ stats the filesystem, and its position in run_scan carries an unpinned ordering
findings.why_it_matters: The ledger names an order no comment or test holds.
findings.chosen: Side A: Add a one-line comment at the construction site

findings.title: The symlinked-base read gate in lookup has no test
findings.why_it_matters: Removing the gate passed the full suite and replayed a forged entry through the symlink.
findings.chosen: Side A: Add one pin now

findings.title: self_ignore stands in for the user giving no --cache-dir, and three behaviours hang off it
findings.why_it_matters: The name hides that the flag is also the trust bit, which matters once #52 adds another location.
findings.chosen: Side A: Leave the name and shape
findings.choice_reason: User asked for a note on #52; posted as a comment there.

findings.title: FilePhaseResult is one more layer than the code needs, but the ledger asked for it
findings.why_it_matters: A dataclass built once and read once, which #59 will reshape.
findings.chosen: Side A: Keep FilePhaseResult as ratified

findings.title: The no-key case is checked in both lookup and store
findings.why_it_matters: A keyed handle would remove both checks at the cost of a new type.
findings.chosen: Side A: Keep the two is-None checks

No pin for --debug plus a cached error forcing a rescan
